key: “The love of a Sage for his fellows likewise finds expression among mankind. Were he not told so, he would not know that he loved his fellows.
s: After the beauty who knows her beauty only when told, the passage turns to the Sage’s love; Guo Xiang, on chapter 25, explains that the Sage, like a mirror, has no love, but his work helps things and people give it that name.
src: Guo Xiang, Zhuangzi zhu, chapter 25, zh.wikisource (the Zhengtong Daozang edition), revision 5978511 (2026)

opened.locator: chapter 25, the note on 聖人之愛人也，人與之名，不告則不知其愛人也 (25.19)

opened.edition: Legge, SBE 40 (1891), OCR notes to Book XXV

evidence.words: 聖人無愛若鏡耳。然而事濟於物，故人與之名，若人不相告，則莫知其愛人也。
evidence.gloss: The Sage has no love, just as a mirror has none. Yet his doings bring things through, so people give him the name; if people did not tell one another, none would know that he loves people.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, Zhuangzi 25.19, at 2646). Guo Xiang’s note on 25.19 says the Sage has no love, like a mirror, but his doings help things, so people give him the name of love. The sentence’s reading follows it closely; the mirror image is Guo Xiang’s own (his note on 25.18 glosses 鑑 as a mirror). Plain sense (the beauty who knows only when told, 25.18, then the Sage’s love) matches the passage. entry-check ok.
